summary.name: How we've evolved on-call at Monzo
summary.one_liner: A Monzo engineering blog post describing the company's tiered, paid on-call process, including primary, shadow and specialist rotas and the in-house Response tool.
use_cases: Designing an on-call rota for an engineering team
Routing alerts directly to owning teams
summary.what_it_does: The post describes how Monzo structures on-call across two tiers: a first-line primary and shadow rota of volunteer engineers, and a second-line specialist rota staffed by members of each domain team. It explains the split between in-hours and out-of-hours rotas, acknowledgement targets (15 minutes for first line, 1 hour for specialists), and weekly pay for on-callers. It also covers routing alerts straight to owning teams where ownership is clear, and mentions Response, an in-house Django tool integrated with Slack that the company has open sourced.
notable: Two-tier on-call with first-line primary/shadow rota and second-line domain specialist rota
On-call engineers are paid weekly, with no per-incident pay
Response, the in-house incident tool, is a Django app that has been open sourced
Alerts route directly to owning teams where ownership is clear
caveats: Alert routing directly to specialists only covers alerts with clear team ownership; many incidents still reach first-line on-callers first
Monzo's pay figures and rota details are specific to its own organisation and may not transfer directly
